title: Spirits from the giants and the demons partially restrained — 1 Enoch 15-16 and Jubilees 10
summary_md: When the two demoniacs at Gergesa cry out, *what have we to do with thee, Yahusha (Jesus), thou Son of Elohim (God)? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?* (Matthew 8:29), they are speaking as creatures who know where they came from and what day is waiting for them. The book of Enoch tells both. The spirits that trouble men are the spirits of the giants, the children the Watchers begot on the daughters of men: *Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; because they are born from men and from the holy Watchers is their beginning and primal origin; they shall be evil spirits on earth, and evil spirits shall they be called.* (1 Enoch 15:9). Their work on the earth is named without softening: *And the spirits of the giants afflict, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, and work destruction on the earth, and cause trouble: they take no food, but nevertheless hunger and thirst, and cause offences.* (1 Enoch 15:11). And they have a day fixed for them, which they know: *From the days of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, from the souls of whose flesh the spirits, having gone forth, shall destroy without incurring judgement—thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great judgement in which the age shall be consummated, over the Watchers and the godless, yea, shall be wholly consummated."* (1 Enoch 16:1). Jubilees carries the story past the flood, when *the unclean demons began to lead astray the children of the sons of Noah; and to make to err and destroy them.* (Jubilees 10:1), and tells how their chief pleaded to keep a portion of them loose: *the chief of the spirits, Mastêmâ, came and said: Yahuah (God), Creator, let some of them remain before me ... for if some of them are not left to me, I shall not be able to execute the power of my will on the sons of men.* (Jubilees 10:8). A tenth part was left him, subject before Satan on the earth, and the rest were bound in the place of condemnation (Jubilees 10:11). So the fear in the demons' mouth at Matthew 8:29 is not a strange outburst. They are the spirits of the giants, left loose for a season, and the one standing in front of them is the Judge of the day Enoch said they would destroy until. They know the time has not yet come, and they know who sets it.

title: Psalm 110:1 — David's Lord, the Formed at the right hand of the Formless
summary_md:
*David himself said by the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), Yahuah (the LORD) said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand* (Mark 12:36). Yahusha (Jesus) puts the question to the temple crowd and lets it hang: David called the Messiah his Lord, so the son of David is more than David's son. The psalm itself says it plainly: *Yahuah (the LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.* (Psalm 110:1). The first Lord is Yahuah speaking; the second is the one David bows to as his own sovereign. One speaks, the other sits at his right hand. That is the Father, who has no form, speaking to the Son, who is his form made visible, and it is Yahusha's own mouth that hands the people the verse in the days before the cross. Peter preaches the same verse at Pentecost (*Yahuah (the LORD) said unto my Lord,* Acts 2:34), Hebrews opens with it (*sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool,* Hebrews 1:13), and Paul carries the footstool forward to the end of the reign (*for he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet,* 1 Corinthians 15:25).

Enoch saw the same throne and the same two figures. The one who sits was named before anything was made: *And at that hour that Son of Adam was named In the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days.* (1 Enoch 48:2). And the Head of Days speaks of him as his own: *On that day Mine Elect One shall sit on the throne of glory And shall try their works, And their places of rest shall be innumerable. And their souls shall grow strong within them when they see Mine elect ones, And those who have called upon My glorious name:* (1 Enoch 45:3). The seat at the right hand is not two gods and it is not one person in two poses. It is the Father and the Son he brought forth, in the relation they have always had, written into the one verse of the Psalms the apostles quote more than any other.

title: Sodom and the Watchers changed the order of nature
summary_md: Naphtali warns his children not to become as Sodom, which changed the order of nature, nor as the Watchers who likewise changed the order of their nature, whom Yahuah (the LORD) cursed at the flood. The Gentiles forsook their Maker and served stocks and stones; the children of Elohim (God) must not. It ain't new — Genesis tells of Sodom and of the sons of Elohim (God) who took wives of the daughters of men, Enoch tells how the Watchers left their own high place and corrupted the earth, and Jude sets both side by side as a warning of the vengeance reserved for them: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he has reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.* (Jude 1:6).
note: READ: the mention of 1 Enoch is a true summary of the book (chs 6-16); left the gloss, restored the names in prose, and added Jude 1:6 from the index so the apostles' warning is on the page

title: The Animal Apocalypse — shepherds judged, new house built, sheep gathered (1 Enoch 90)
summary_md: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36). Ezekiel had already told Yashar'el (Israel) whose fault that was: *Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I am against the shepherds; and I will require my flock at their hand, and cause them to cease from feeding the flock; neither shall the shepherds feed themselves any more; for I will deliver my flock from their mouth, that they may not be meat for them.* (Ezekiel 34:10), and he had promised the one shepherd who would take their place: *And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.* (Ezekiel 34:23). Enoch saw the whole of it in his second dream, where the flock is given over to seventy shepherds who kill more than they were told to. When the Lord of the sheep comes, the record is opened first: *And I saw that man, who wrote the book according to the command of Yahuah (Lord), till he opened that book concerning the destruction which those twelve last shepherds had wrought, and showed that they had destroyed much more than their predecessors, before Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:17). Then the shepherds answer for the flock: *And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were cast into that fiery abyss.* (1 Enoch 90:25). Then the old house is folded up and a new one set in its place: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep brought a new house greater and loftier than that first, and set it up in the place of the first which had been folded up: all its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and larger than those of the first, the old one which He had taken away, and all the sheep were within it.* (1 Enoch 90:29). And the scattered come home to it: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). So when Yahusha (Jesus) looks at the crowds and sees sheep with no shepherd, he is looking at the flock Ezekiel described and Enoch watched, and he is the shepherd both of them said would come for it.

title: The blood of Hevel (Abel) crying and the mother hen gathering — 1 Enoch 22 and 2 Esdras 1 beside Matthew 23:29-39
summary_md: The seventh woe ends with blood. *That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom you slew between the temple and the altar.* (Matthew 23:35). Yahusha (Jesus) reaches back to the first murder and forward to the last one recorded in the Hebrew order of the books, and lays the whole line of slain prophets at the feet of the men who were building the prophets' tombs. The ground had been crying the whole time: *And he said, What have you done? the voice of your brother's blood cries unto me from the ground.* (Genesis 4:10). Enoch was shown where that cry goes. In the mountain in the west, among the hollow places where the souls of the dead wait for the day of judgement, one voice goes up louder than the rest: *I saw the spirits of the children of men who were dead, and their voice went forth to heaven and made suit. Then I asked Raphael the angel who was with me, and I said unto him: 'This spirit—whose is it, whose voice goeth forth and maketh suit?' And he answered me saying: 'This is the spirit which went forth from Abel, whom his brother Cain slew, and he makes his suit against him till his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is annihilated from amongst the seed of men.'* (1 Enoch 22:5-7). Abel is still making his suit, and it is a suit against a seed, not against one man. That is why the woe is addressed to *you serpents, you generation of vipers* (Matthew 23:33). The men who killed the prophets and were about to kill the Son are the seed Abel's blood has been pleading against since the field outside Eden, sown in among the people and wearing the priest's robe, and the judgement that falls on them is not a judgement on the Yahudim (Jews) as a people. The same chapter of Enoch shows the hollow places divided, the righteous by their spring of water, the sinners kept for the great day, and those who were slain making their disclosure against the ones who slew them, so the damnation of Gehenna the woe names is a holding and a judgement, not the endless torture the pulpit painted over it. Then the voice changes. *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto you, how often would I have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not!* (Matthew 23:37). Ezra had heard the Father say the same thing in the same words, that he gathered them as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, that he sent them prophets whom they took and slew, and that their house is desolate (2 Esdras 1:30-33). The Son speaks with the Father's own voice and the Father's own grief. The judgement on the shepherds is what clears the ground for the gathering, as Ezekiel 34 lays it out, and the lament is not a door shut on the city. It is the Father's heart toward the children of the broken-off, who will yet be brought home out of the nations the way the prophets said they would be.

title: The corrupted priesthood and the proselyte made twofold — Testament of Levi, 1 Enoch 99, Wisdom of Solomon beside Matthew 23:13-22
summary_md: The first three woes are aimed at a priesthood. They shut up the kingdom of heaven against men and will not go in themselves, they split hairs over which oath binds and which does not, and in between those two stands the woe that names what the whole system was doing: *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, you make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.* (Matthew 23:15). The proselyte was told that becoming a Yahudi (Jew) by the rite would save him, and then he was handed a Torah buried under traditions that voided it, so he ended up worse off than the men who made him. Paul fights the same gospel in Galatia a generation later, and it is still being preached today under other names, wherever a system tells a man that joining it is salvation and then teaches him against the commandments. Enoch had already described the men who do this: *Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness, And transgress the eternal law, And transform themselves into what they were not [into sinners]: They shall be trodden under foot upon the earth.* (1 Enoch 99:2). Perverting the words of uprightness while transgressing the eternal law is the proselyte-maker's trade exactly, and the man he makes is transformed into what he was not. The Testament of Levi had warned the priests themselves that they would deal lawlessly with Yashar'el (Israel) until the veil of the temple was rent, and that the priests of the last times would be idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud and lawless, and the Wisdom of Solomon tells the ministers of the kingdom that they will be judged because they did not judge aright nor keep the law. The test is the same one John gives: whoever says he knows him and does not keep his commandments is a liar. Hold that against any priesthood, in any age, and the woes find their mark. The mark is the system, not the people under it. The King speaking the woes is himself a Yahudi (Jew), so are the apostles, so are the crowds in front of him, and the chapter ends not with their rejection but with his lament over the children he would have gathered.

title: The days of Noach (Noah) and the judgement that took them all away — 1 Enoch 10, 65, 67 and Jubilees 5 beside Matthew 24:37-39
summary_md: *But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be. For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:37-39). Yahusha (Jesus) does not pick the flood at random. The days of Noah are the days the Watchers had corrupted the earth, and the whole book of Enoch is the record of how that judgement was decided and carried out. The warning to Noah comes first: *'Go to Noah and tell him in my name "Hide thyself!" and reveal to him the end that is approaching: that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a deluge is about to come upon the whole earth, and will destroy all that is on it.* (1 Enoch 10:2). The reason is spelled out to him later by his grandfather: *And He said unto me: "Because of their unrighteousness their judgement has been determined upon and shall not be withheld by Me for ever. Because of the sorceries which they have searched out and learnt, the earth and those who dwell upon it shall be destroyed."* (1 Enoch 65:10), and the ones who taught the sorceries are given their own sentence: *And He will imprison those angels, who have shown unrighteousness, in that burning valley which my grandfather Enoch had formerly shown to me in the west among the mountains of gold and silver and iron and soft metal and tin.* (1 Enoch 67:4). Jubilees describes the same earth: *And lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way, alike men and cattle and beasts and birds and everything that walks on the earth-all of them corrupted their ways and their orders, and they began to devour each other, and lawlessness increased on the earth and every imagination of the thoughts of all men (was) thus evil continually.* (Jubilees 5:2). Lawlessness abounding is the very sign Yahusha gives for the end of the age a few verses earlier, when the love of many grows cold. So read the taking in the flood's own terms. The flood took away the ones who were not ready; it did not lift them out of trouble. When the Son of Adam comes, the one taken from the field and the one taken from the mill are taken the way the flood took the world of Noah's day, and Luke's disciples ask where, and are told where the body is, there the eagles gather. Noah and his seed were the ones preserved, kept through the judgement and not carried off by it, and Enoch hears the promise over them: *And I will make fast thy seed before me for ever and ever, and I will spread abroad those who dwell with thee: it shall not be unfruitful on the face of the earth, but it shall be blessed and multiply on the earth in the name of Yahuah (Lord).'* (1 Enoch 67:3). Jude says the whole thing in one line, quoting Enoch himself: *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) comes with ten thousands of his saints,* (Jude 1:14).

title: The Elect One at the right hand — the Parables of Enoch beside David's Lord at Matthew 22:41-46
summary_md: *Saying, What think you of Messiah (Christ)? whose son is he? They say unto him, The Son of David. He says unto them, How then does David in spirit call him the Lord, saying, Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit you on my right hand, till I make your enemies your footstool? If David then call him the Lord, how is he his son?* (Matthew 22:42-45). Nobody in the temple could answer him, and from that day no one dared ask him another question. The question stands on two Lords in one verse. The first is Yahuah, the Father who has no form. The second is the one David bows to, and he sits at the Father's right hand because the Father seats him there. Enoch saw this before David wrote it. He saw an old one with a head of days, and beside him another whose face was like a man's, and asked who he was: *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3). This Son of Adam is older than David's line, older than the stars: *And at that hour that Son of Adam was named In the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days.* (1 Enoch 48:2). And the throne is given, not seized: *And the Elect One shall in those days sit on My throne, And his mouth shall pour forth all the secrets of wisdom and counsel: For Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath given (them) to him and hath glorified him.* (1 Enoch 51:3); *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits placed the Elect One on the throne of glory. And he shall judge all the works of the holy above in the heaven, And in the balance shall their deeds be weighed.* (1 Enoch 61:8). Put the psalm and the Parables side by side and the answer to the temple's riddle is plain. The son of David is greater than David because he was named before the Head of Days before David's house existed, and he is not the Father, because the Father is the one who names him and seats him. He was hidden from the beginning and shown to the elect: *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). John says the same thing in his first line: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).* (John 1:1). So the Son is not a creature made at a point in time, and he is not the Father wearing another face, and he is not one of three equals; he is the Father's own form, brought forth from him and seated by him, which is why the whole apostolic witness keeps coming back to this psalm, from Peter at Pentecost to Hebrews to the Revelation.

title: The Elect One on the throne and the keys of the kingdom — 1 Enoch 49, 51, 62 and 69 beside Matthew 16:19
summary_md: *And I will give unto you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever you shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever you shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.* (Matthew 16:19). A steward can only hand out keys that belong to the house he serves, so the question behind the verse is whose house it is and who holds the judgement the keys administer. Enoch answers from the throne room. The Elect One stands before the Father and is given the secrets: *For he is mighty in all the secrets of righteousness, And unrighteousness shall disappear as a shadow, And have no continuance; Because the Elect One standeth before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And his glory is for ever and ever, And his might unto all generations.* (1 Enoch 49:2). He sits on the Father's throne and what he pours out is wisdom, not his own invention: *And the Elect One shall in those days sit on My throne, And his mouth shall pour forth all the secrets of wisdom and counsel: For Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath given (them) to him and hath glorified him.* (1 Enoch 51:3). He was kept hidden and then shown to the elect: *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). And the whole of judgement is put into his hands: *And he sat on the throne of his glory, And the sum of judgement was given unto the Son of Adam, And he caused the sinners to pass away and be destroyed from off the face of the earth, And those who have led the world astray.* (1 Enoch 69:27). John heard the same from his own mouth: *For the Father judges no man, but has committed all judgment unto the Son:* (John 5:22), *And has given him authority to execute judgment also, because he is the Son of Adam.* (John 5:27). That is the throne the keys come down from. Isaiah had shown the pattern already in Shebna and Eliakim, the self-appointed steward put out of the house and the key of David laid on the shoulder of the one the Master chose. The scribes and priests of the second temple were Shebna; the twelve were Eliakim; and what Peter received was a stewardship under the Son's judgement, binding and loosing what the Master of the house had already bound and loosed. Any church that reads the verse as a licence to define doctrine against the Word of the house has mistaken the steward for the owner.

title: The Elect One vindicated on the throne and the kings and the mighty condemned — 1 Enoch 46, 48, 62 and 63 beside Matthew 26:64
summary_md: Bound and under oath before the high priest, Yahusha (Jesus) answers with the two verses the Sanhedrin knew best: *Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, You have said: nevertheless I say unto you, Hereafter shall you see the Son of Adam sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.* (Matthew 26:64). Sitting at the right hand is David's psalm; coming in the clouds is Daniel's night vision: *I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* (Daniel 7:13). Daniel says the figure was like a son of Adam, because the one he saw was going to take on flesh; the man in front of Caiaphas is the one Daniel's figure resembled, and he says so with the title and no comparison. Enoch had seen him by name beside the Head of Days: *And I asked the angel who went with me and showed me all the hidden things, concerning that Son of Adam, who he was, and whence he was, (and) why he went with the Head of Days?* (1 Enoch 46:2), and he had been told what this Son of Adam would do to men who sit in judgement seats: *And this Son of Adam whom thou hast seen Shall raise up the kings and the mighty from their seats, [And the strong from their thrones] And shall loosen the reins of the strong, And break the teeth of the sinners.* (1 Enoch 46:4). He was named before anything they ruled over was made: *Yea, before the sun and the signs were created, Before the stars of the heaven were made, His name was named before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 48:3). So the court that condemned him that night will one day stand in his: *And all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the earth Shall fall down before him on their faces, And worship and set their hope upon that Son of Adam, And petition him and supplicate for mercy at his hands.* (1 Enoch 62:9). Enoch even records what they will say when it is too late: *And splendid in every secret thing is Thy power from generation to generation, And Thy glory for ever and ever: Deep are all Thy secrets and innumerable, And Thy righteousness is beyond reckoning.* (1 Enoch 63:3). Isaiah swore the same oath for the Father, *That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.* (Isaiah 45:23), and Paul puts it on the name of Yahusha: *That at the name of Yahusha (Jesus) every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth;* (Philippians 2:10). The ones who will bow are the kings and the mighty, the leadership that persecuted the houses of his congregations, not the Yahudim (Jews) as a people. The King on trial is of the tribe of Yahudah (Judah) himself, and so are the men who followed him out of that courtyard.

title: The gates of Sheol and the dead given back — Wisdom of Solomon, 1 Enoch 51 and 2 Esdras 4 beside Matthew 16:18
summary_md: *And I say also unto you, That you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.* (Matthew 16:18). The gates of hell are the gates of Sheol, the grave, the place where the dead are held. The pulpit turned the phrase into the mouth of an everlasting furnace, but the library that Yahusha (Jesus) grew up in uses it for the power of death that came in with the curse. The Wisdom of Solomon says that Elohim (God) made not death, and has no pleasure in the destruction of the living, and that he has power of life and death, leads down to the gates of hell and brings up again. Hosea had the Father say it in his own voice: *I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be your plagues; O grave, I will be your destruction: repentance shall be hid from my eyes.* (Hosea 13:14). And Enoch was shown the day the gates give way: *And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes.* (1 Enoch 51:1). Ezra heard the righteous waiting for that day in their chambers: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). So the promise to the assembly is a resurrection promise. The grave will take its members the way it takes everyone, and it will not be allowed to keep them, because the one who builds the assembly is the one who walked out of the tomb on the third day and holds the keys: *I am he that lives, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.* (Revelation 1:18). The assembly shares in his rising at the first resurrection, and Sheol gives back what it owes.

title: The gathering of the elect from the four winds — 1 Enoch 57, 61 and 90 beside Matthew 24:27-31
summary_md: *For as the lightning comes out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:27). There is nothing secret about it. He comes in the clouds with power and great glory, and then the trumpet sounds: *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31). Enoch heard that sound from end to end of heaven in the second Parable: *And it came to pass after this that I saw another host of wagons, and men riding thereon, and coming on the winds from the east, and from the west to the south. And the noise of their wagons was heard, and when this turmoil took place the holy ones from heaven remarked it, and the pillars of the earth were moved from their place, and the sound thereof was heard from the one end of heaven to the other, in one day.* (1 Enoch 57:1-2). And he was told that none of the elect will be missed in the gathering, not even the ones the earth had swallowed: *And these measures shall reveal all the secrets of the depths of the earth, And those who have been destroyed by the desert, And those who have been devoured by the beasts, And those who have been devoured by the fish of the sea, That they may return and stay themselves On the day of the Elect One; For none shall be destroyed before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And none can be destroyed.* (1 Enoch 61:5). In the dream of the sheep the same gathering closes the vision: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). The elect gathered from the four winds are the sheep, the house of Yashar'el (Israel) scattered through every nation, the ones the prophets never stopped promising to bring home: *And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.* (Isaiah 11:12); *And say unto them, Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:* (Ezekiel 37:21). Moses, Jeremiah, Hosea, Micah, Zephaniah and Zechariah say the same thing in their own places. The gathering at the trumpet is the gathering of the twelve tribes, the paternal seed of the fathers, and not a spiritual category anyone can elect himself into.

title: The judgment of the kings and the mighty cast down — the Parables of Enoch beside the sheep and the goats at Matthew 25:31-46
summary_md: *When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats:* (Matthew 25:31-32). The throne of his glory is Enoch's phrase, and the Parables show who is standing in front of it. *And there shall stand up in that day all the kings and the mighty, And the exalted and those who hold the earth, And they shall see and recognize How he sits on the throne of his glory, And righteousness is judged before him, And no lying word is spoken before him.* (1 Enoch 62:3). The sight of him is what undoes them: *And one portion of them shall look on the other, And they shall be terrified, And they shall be downcast of countenance, And pain shall seize them, When they see that Son of Adam Sitting on the throne of his glory.* (1 Enoch 62:5). They bow too late: *And all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the earth Shall fall down before him on their faces, And worship and set their hope upon that Son of Adam, And petition him and supplicate for mercy at his hands.* (1 Enoch 62:9), and they are handed over: *And He will deliver them to the angels for punishment, To execute vengeance on them because they have oppressed His children and His elect* (1 Enoch 62:11). Enoch even records their confession from the darkness: *For we have not believed before Him Nor glorified the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, [nor glorified our Lord] But our hope was in the sceptre of our kingdom, And in our glory.* (1 Enoch 63:7). That is the goats' *Lord, when saw we thee* in another tongue, the recognition that comes after the door is shut. The fire the goats are sent toward was never made for them in the first place: *Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:* (Matthew 25:41). It was prepared for the Watchers and their master, and Jude and Peter say the same. The goats are the unfruitful among the gathered, sifted out before the reign; the kings and the mighty who possess the earth fall at the Day with the tares abroad; and the verdict is final, *And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.* (Matthew 25:46). There is no universal rescue hidden in the chapter, and there is no endless torture of the uninformed either. There is a throne, a shepherd who knows his sheep, and a door that closes.

title: The kings and the mighty condemning the Elect One, and the Elect One vindicated on the throne of his glory — 1 Enoch 62-63 beside Matthew 27
summary_md: *When the morning was come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Yahusha (Jesus) to put him to death:* (Matthew 27:1). David had seen that council: *The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed, saying,* (Psalm 2:2). By the afternoon the same men are under the cross: *He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Yashar'el (Israel), let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him. He trusted in Elohim (God); let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of Elohim (God).* (Matthew 27:42-43). Enoch saw the other end of that scene. He saw the day the kings and the mighty are summoned to look at the one they condemned: *And thus Yahuah (Lord) commanded the kings and the mighty and the exalted, and those who dwell on the earth, and said: 'Open your eyes and lift up your horns if ye are able to recognize the Elect One.'* (1 Enoch 62:1); *And there shall stand up in that day all the kings and the mighty, And the exalted and those who hold the earth, And they shall see and recognize How he sits on the throne of his glory, And righteousness is judged before him, And no lying word is spoken before him.* (1 Enoch 62:3). He could have called twelve legions of angels at Gethsemane and did not, because the one who was hidden from the beginning was walking the road the Father laid for him: *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). His cry from the cross is the opening line of Psalm 22, and that psalm does not end forsaken; it ends with the Father hearing and all the ends of the earth turning to him. The Father did not abandon the Son; the Son prayed the psalm the way the Suffering Servant was always going to pray it, through to its end. And the men who mocked will one day beg for a moment's respite: *In those days shall the mighty and the kings who possess the earth implore (Him) to grant them a little respite from His angels of punishment to whom they were delivered, that they might fall down and worship before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, and confess their sins before Him.* (1 Enoch 63:1), and they will say what they refused to say at Golgotha: *And splendid in every secret thing is Thy power from generation to generation, And Thy glory for ever and ever: Deep are all Thy secrets and innumerable, And Thy righteousness is beyond reckoning.* (1 Enoch 63:3). Paul says every knee will bow at the name of Yahusha, things in heaven, in earth and under the earth. The cross and the throne are the same figure seen from two days.

title: The Lord of the sheep and the gathering — 1 Enoch 40 and 89-90 beside Matthew 18:10-14
summary_md: *Take heed that you despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven. For the Son of Adam is come to save that which was lost.* (Matthew 18:10-11). Then comes the shepherd who leaves the ninety and nine on the mountains to go after the one that strayed, and the Father's will that not one of these little ones should perish. Enoch saw the angels who stand before that face. *And he said to me: 'This first is Michael, the merciful and long- suffering: and the second, who is set over all the diseases and all the wounds of the children of men, is Raphael: and the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel: and the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel.'* (1 Enoch 40:9). And in the dream of the sheep he saw the Shepherd himself, called by the name Yahuah. When the wolves of Egypt oppressed the flock, the sheep cried to their Lord, and he came down for them: *And a sheep which had been saved from the wolves fled and escaped to the wild asses; and I saw the sheep how they lamented and cried, and besought their Lord with all their might, till that Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep descended at the voice of the sheep from a lofty abode, and came to them and pastured them.* (1 Enoch 89:16). The same Lord raises up a shepherd when the beasts devour the flock, *And the dogs and the foxes and the wild boars began to devour those sheep till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep raised up [another sheep] a ram from their midst, which led them.* (1 Enoch 89:42), and when the sheep forsake his house and are given over, Enoch watches until the day the eyes of the lambs come open: *But behold lambs were borne by those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and to see, and to cry to the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:6). At the end the Lord of the sheep acts for them with his own hand: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep came unto them and took in His hand the staff of His wrath, and smote the earth, and the earth clave asunder, and all the beasts and all the birds of the heaven fell from among those sheep, and were swallowed up in the earth and it covered them.* (1 Enoch 90:18). This is Ezekiel 34 in a dream, the Father against the shepherds who fed themselves and the one Shepherd who comes to seek the lost. The parable in Matthew works at both levels at once: the little one in the assembly who must not be despised, and the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) he said he was sent to. Both belong to the same Lord of the sheep, and the lambs whose eyes open are the ones who hear his voice when he calls, because they are his.

title: The named Son of Adam — 1 Enoch 46 and Matthew 8:20
summary_md: *And Yahusha (Jesus) says unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Adam has not where to lay his head.* (Matthew 8:20). It is the first time in Matthew that he calls himself by that name, and he uses it as a title, not as a way of saying he is only a man. The English Bibles flattened it to *son of man* and the lineage went out of it; *ben adam* is the son of Adam, the seed of the line the promise runs through. Enoch had already seen a figure called by that title standing beside the Ancient of Days: *And there I saw One who had a head of days, And His head was white like wool, And with Him was another being whose countenance had the appearance of a man, And his face was full of graciousness, like one of the holy angels.* (1 Enoch 46:1). He asked who he was: *And I asked the angel who went with me and showed me all the hidden things, concerning that Son of Adam, who he was, and whence he was, (and) why he went with the Head of Days?* (1 Enoch 46:2). And he was told: *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3). Chosen by the Father, given the first place in righteousness for ever, the one who reveals what is hidden, standing at the Father's side before he ever came in flesh: that is the Messiah in heaven before the manger. The one Enoch saw with the Head of Days is the one who told the scribe he had nowhere to lay his head. Daniel saw him too, coming with the clouds like a son of Adam, and said like, because the one he saw was going to take on flesh. Here there is no like. He names himself.

title: The named Son of Adam in the Parables of Enoch — named before the stars, hidden, and revealed, beside Matthew 9:6
summary_md: *But that you may know that the Son of Adam has power on earth to forgive sins, (then says he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up your bed, and go unto your house.* (Matthew 9:6). The scribes had just said in their hearts that only Elohim (God) can forgive sins, and they were right about that. What they did not know was who was standing in the room. Enoch had been shown him long before, and shown that his name was older than the lights in the sky: *And at that hour that Son of Adam was named In the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days. Yea, before the sun and the signs were created, Before the stars of the heaven were made, His name was named before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 48:2-3). He was kept out of sight until the Father chose to show him: *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). The man in Capernaum who tells a paralytic his sins are forgiven and then proves it by telling him to walk is the one named before the stars, the one the Father kept hidden and then revealed. The authority to forgive is not something he borrowed for the afternoon; it belongs to the one who sits on the Father's throne, and he exercises it in flesh on a street in Galilee. Matthew 8:20 gave the title at the first; here the title does what only Elohim (God) does.

title: The resurrection of the righteous — 2 Maccabees 7's mother and seven sons, 2 Esdras and the Wisdom of Solomon beside Matthew 22:23-33
summary_md: The Sadducees, the priestly families who held the temple and denied the resurrection, bring Yahusha (Jesus) a riddle built on the levirate law, seven brothers and one wife, to make the resurrection look absurd. He tells them they err because they know neither the scriptures nor the power of Elohim (God), and he answers from the bush: *I am the Elohim (God) of Avraham (Abraham), and the Elohim (God) of Yitschaq (Isaac), and the Elohim (God) of Ya'aqov (Jacob); Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.* (Matthew 22:32). The fathers are asleep, not gone, and the one who spoke to Moses still calls himself theirs. His word about the angels is about the angels who stayed in heaven; the ones Enoch writes of left it and took wives, which is the whole reason Genesis 6 and Jude 6 are in the Bible, so the verse is not a rule about every angel that ever was. The martyrs under Antiochus had already confessed what the Sadducees denied. The second of the seven sons told the king that the King of the world would raise them up to everlasting life, because they died for his laws, and their mother told them that the Creator who gave them breath would give it back again (2 Maccabees 7:9, 23). Ezra was shown the same day: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32), which is Daniel's word carried forward: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2). And the Wisdom of Solomon tells where the righteous are in the meantime: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). Read that whole chapter and the shining and the judging of nations it promises belong to the day of their visitation, the resurrection, not to a disembodied soul flying off at the moment of death. The righteous sleep in the Father's keeping and wait for the one who comes to raise them, which is what Paul tells the grieving at Thessalonica, and what John calls the first resurrection. The seven brothers and their mother paid in blood for a hope the Sadducees mocked, and it is the same hope the Sadducees' own scriptures held.

title: The Son of Adam came to give his life a ransom for many — the Parables of Enoch, the Testament of Benjamin and Sirach beside Matthew 20:28
summary_md: *Even as the Son of Adam came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.* (Matthew 20:28). The sons of Zebedee had asked for the seats on his right and his left, and he answers by turning the whole order of greatness upside down: whoever would be great must serve, and he says it of himself first. The title he uses makes the saying heavier than it sounds. The Son of Adam is the one Enoch saw beside the Head of Days: *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3), named before anything was made: *And at that hour that Son of Adam was named In the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days.* (1 Enoch 48:2). The ransom was settled that early too; John calls him the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. And the one who gives his life is the one the kings will one day beg mercy of: *And all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the earth Shall fall down before him on their faces, And worship and set their hope upon that Son of Adam, And petition him and supplicate for mercy at his hands.* (1 Enoch 62:9). The same figure who serves at the first coming judges at the second. The ransom is the Torah's own word, the price paid for a life, and the *many* are Isaiah's many: *He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities.* (Isaiah 53:11); *Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he has poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.* (Isaiah 53:12). Not everyone without distinction, and not a handful picked at random, but the many whose names the Father wrote. The Testament of Benjamin had said the Most High would be lowly on earth and glorious in heaven, and Sirach that the greater a man is the more he must humble himself. The King took the lowest place in the room on purpose, because that is where the ransom gets paid.

title: The Son of Adam named before the Head of Days, revealing the treasures of that which is hidden — 1 Enoch 46-48 beside Matthew 11:25-27
summary_md: *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank you, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because you have hid these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25), and then: *All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.* (Matthew 11:27). Hidden, then revealed, and revealed by the Son to whom he chooses. Enoch watched that same arrangement in heaven. He saw the Father, with a head of days and hair white like wool, and beside him one whose face was like a man's and full of grace (1 Enoch 46:1), and was told who he was: *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3). The Son himself was hidden first: *And for this reason hath he been chosen and hidden before Him, Before the creation of the world and for evermore.* (1 Enoch 48:6). And the ones he is shown to are not the wise of this world: *And the wisdom of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath revealed him to the holy and righteous; For he hath preserved the lot of the righteous, Because they have hated and despised this world of unrighteousness, And have hated all its works and ways in the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits: For in his name they are saved, And according to his good pleasure hath it been in regard to their life.* (1 Enoch 48:7). The babes of the prayer are the holy and righteous of the Parable, the ones the Father preserved and chose to show his Son to. What Enoch saw in a vision, the Word made flesh says out loud on a road in Galilee, thanking the Father for working exactly that way.

title: The Son of the living Elohim named before the foundation — 1 Enoch 46 and 48, and Wisdom of Solomon 2, beside Matthew 16:13-17
summary_md: *When Yahusha (Jesus) came into the coasts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of Adam am?* (Matthew 16:13). He asks it with the title already in his mouth. Peter answers, *You are the Messiah (Christ), the Son of the living Elohim (God).* (Matthew 16:16), and is told where the answer came from: *Blessed are you, Simon Bar-jona: for flesh and blood has not revealed it unto you, but my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 16:17). Enoch had asked the same question of the angel who walked with him: *And I asked the angel who went with me and showed me all the hidden things, concerning that Son of Adam, who he was, and whence he was, (and) why he went with the Head of Days?* (1 Enoch 46:2), and got the same kind of answer, from heaven: *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3). And he was told how old the name is: *And at that hour that Son of Adam was named In the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days. Yea, before the sun and the signs were created, Before the stars of the heaven were made, His name was named before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 48:2-3). The Wisdom of Solomon had the wicked say of the just man that if he is the son of Elohim (God), he will help him and deliver him out of their hands, and they would prove it by his death, which is exactly what the chief priests said under the cross. Peter did not work the confession out by watching miracles. The Father showed him what had been true since before the stars, and Peter said it. That is how it always goes: the sheep hear because they are sheep, and the Father reveals what he settled before the foundation of the world.

title: The Two Ways of Enoch and the narrow gate
summary_md: *Enter you in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leads unto life, and few there be that find it.* (Matthew 7:13-14). Two ways and no third one. Moses set them in front of Yashar'el (Israel) at the edge of the land: *See, I have set before you this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both you and your seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter opens on the same fork: *For Yahuah (LORD) knows the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalm 1:6), and Jeremiah set it before a city under siege: *And unto this people you shall say, Thus says Yahuah (LORD); Behold, I set before you the way of life, and the way of death.* (Jeremiah 21:8). Enoch gave it to his sons as his last instruction: *And now I say unto you, my sons, love righteousness and walk therein; For the paths of righteousness are worthy of acceptation, But the paths of unrighteousness shall suddenly be destroyed and vanish.* (1 Enoch 94:1). He also knew that some would see both roads and still walk the wrong one: *And to certain men of a generation shall the paths of violence and of death be revealed, And they shall hold themselves afar from them, And shall not follow them.* (1 Enoch 94:2), *And now I say unto you the righteous: Walk not in the paths of wickedness, nor in the paths of death, And draw not nigh to them, lest ye be destroyed.* (1 Enoch 94:3). The Sermon on the Mount does not invent the two ways; it hands them back to the people they were given to, and binds them to what follows in the chapter, the ones who say Lord, Lord and are told to depart, and the two builders. The narrow way is the way of the commandments Moses set before them, and the few who find it are the ones who walk in it.

title: The Watchers' rebellion and the first stumbling-blocks — 1 Enoch 8, 10, 19, 22 and 27 beside Matthew 18:6-9
summary_md: *But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea. Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence comes!* (Matthew 18:6-7). The word is a stumbling-block, something laid in the road to trip a walker, and Yahusha (Jesus) says they are bound to come. Enoch tells where the first ones were laid. *And Azâzêl taught men to make swords, and knives, and shields, and breastplates, and made known to them the metals of the earth and the art of working them, and bracelets, and ornaments, and the use of antimony, and the beautifying of the eyelids, and all kinds of costly stones, and all colouring tinctures.* (1 Enoch 8:1). Weapons for the hand and paint for the eye, taught by a fallen angel, and the whole world tripped over them: *And the whole earth has been corrupted through the works that were taught by Azâzêl: to him ascribe all sin.'* (1 Enoch 10:8). The spirits that came out of that rebellion are still laying stones in the road: *And Uriel said to me: 'Here shall stand the angels who have connected themselves with women, and their spirits assuming many different forms are defiling mankind and shall lead them astray into sacrificing to demons as gods, (here shall they stand,) till the day of the great judgement in which they shall be judged till they are made an end of.* (1 Enoch 19:1). Many different forms. Every system that teaches men against the commandments of their Maker, in whatever robe, is one of those forms, and the woe lands on the men who run it, not on the little ones tripped by it. The judgement that makes the millstone look like mercy is the one Enoch saw: *Here their spirits shall be set apart in this great pain till the great day of judgement and punishment and torment of those who curse for ever and retribution for their spirits. There He shall bind them for ever.* (1 Enoch 22:11). And the valley Yahusha names, Gehenna, the valley of Hinnom on the south side of Jerusalem, Enoch had already been shown in the middle of the holy mountain: *Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said: 'This accursed valley is for those who are accursed for ever: Here shall all the accursed be gathered together who utter with their lips against Yahuah (Lord) unseemly words and of His glory speak hard things. Here shall they be gathered together, and here shall be their place of judgement.* (1 Enoch 27:2). That is what the hell fire of Matthew 18:9 is, the accursed valley of judgement the prophets and Enoch knew, and not the endless furnace the pulpit read back into the word. Better to lose a hand than to walk into that valley with both.

title: Thy name and thy throne in the Enochic prayers
summary_md: *After this manner therefore pray you: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.* (Matthew 6:9-10). The holy name, the throne, the kingdom and the will done on earth are the oldest prayer in the library, prayed before Abraham. When the four archangels looked down on the blood the Watchers' sons were shedding, they prayed it: *And they said to Yahuah (Lord) of the ages: 'Lord of lords, Elohim (God) of gods, King of kings, and Elohim (God) of the ages, the throne of Thy glory (standeth) unto all the generations of the ages, and Thy name holy and glorious and blessed unto all the ages!* (1 Enoch 9:4), *Thou hast made all things, and power over all things hast Thou: and all things are naked and open in Thy sight, and Thou seest all things, and nothing can hide itself from Thee.* (1 Enoch 9:5). And Enoch prayed it himself, with the breath of his mouth and the tongue of flesh, when he saw the flood coming: *'Blessed be Thou, O Yahuah (Lord), King, Great and mighty in Thy greatness, Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation of the heaven, King of kings and Elohim (God) of the whole world. And Thy power and kingship and greatness abide for ever and ever, And throughout all generations Thy dominion; And all the heavens are Thy throne for ever, And the whole earth Thy footstool for ever and ever.* (1 Enoch 84:2), *For Thou hast made and Thou rulest all things, And nothing is too hard for Thee, Wisdom departs not from the place of Thy throne, Nor turns away from Thy presence. And Thou knowest and seest and hearest everything, And there is nothing hidden from Thee [for Thou seest everything].* (1 Enoch 84:3). He goes on to ask for exactly what the Lord's Prayer asks, that the Father's will be done on the earth: destroy the flesh that aroused thy wrath, but establish the flesh of righteousness as a plant of the eternal seed. Ezekiel's promise to hallow the great name among the nations and Daniel's kingdom handed to the Son of Adam carry the same prayer in the canon. When Yahusha (Jesus) taught his disciples to pray, he gave them words the heavens had been praying since the days of Jared.

title: Unclean spirits recognize the Holy One of Elohim before the people do
summary_md: Twice in Mark 1-3 the unclean spirits cry out and name what the watching crowds cannot yet say: *And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, You are the Son of Elohim (God).* (Mark 3:11); *Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with you, you Yahusha (Jesus) of Nazareth? are you come to destroy us? I know you who you are, the Holy One of Elohim (God).* (Mark 1:24). They know him because of where they came from. Enoch says the evil spirits on the earth are the spirits of the giants, born of the Watchers who left heaven: *Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; because they are born from men and from the holy Watchers is their beginning and primal origin; they shall be evil spirits on earth, and evil spirits shall they be called.* (1 Enoch 15:9), and they know the day fixed for them: *From the days of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, from the souls of whose flesh the spirits, having gone forth, shall destroy without incurring judgement—thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great judgement in which the age shall be consummated, over the Watchers and the godless, yea, shall be wholly consummated."* (1 Enoch 16:1). Their fathers stood in heaven before the rebellion. They recognize the Formed one when he walks into a synagogue because they have seen him before. James says the devils also believe, and tremble, and that is the whole difference: a demon's recognition is not a sheep's hearing. The Son of Adam silences them, *Hold thy peace,* and charges them not to make him known, because the kingdom is not announced on the testimony of an unclean spirit. It is announced through the prophets, the apostles, and the sheep who hear his voice.

title: The Watchers' corruption as tares sown in the wheat — 1 Enoch 6, 10, 15 and Jubilees 5, 7 beside Matthew 13:25-39
summary_md: *But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.* (Matthew 13:25). When the disciples ask what it means, Yahusha (Jesus) says the tares are a seed with a father: *The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one; The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels.* (Matthew 13:38-39). Enoch records the sowing. *And the angels, the children of the heaven, saw and lusted after them, and said to one another: 'Come, let us choose us wives from among the children of men and beget us children.'* (1 Enoch 6:2). Two hundred of them swore it on Hermon in the days of Jared, and what they begot was a line, not a mood: *And to Gabriel said Yahuah (Lord): 'Proceed against the bastards and the reprobates, and against the children of fornication: and destroy [the children of fornication and] the children of the Watchers from amongst men [and cause them to go forth]: send them one against the other that they may destroy each other in battle: for length of days shall they not have.* (1 Enoch 10:9). Their bodies died in the flood but their spirits stayed: *And now, the giants, who are produced from the spirits and flesh, shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and on the earth shall be their dwelling.* (1 Enoch 15:8). Jubilees is the second witness: *And it came to pass when the children of men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them, that the angels of Elohim (God) saw them on a certain year of this jubilee, that they were beautiful to look upon; and they took themselves wives of all whom they chose, and they bare to them sons and they were giants.* (Jubilees 5:1), and Noah tells his sons that the flood came *owing to the fornication wherein the Watchers against the law of their ordinances went a whoring after the daughters of men, and took themselves wives of all which they chose: and they made the beginning of uncleanness.* (Jubilees 7:21). So the children of the wicked one are a seed sown into the world, and the parable is not a figure of speech about bad attitudes. But hold the other half of it just as firmly. The seed runs inside every people, not along the lines of any nation or color, and Eli's own sons were sons of Belial; nobody can sort the field by looking at it. That is why the servants are told to let both grow together. The sorting belongs to the reapers at the harvest, and to no one else.

title: Wheat from chaff and righteous from wicked at the day of separation — 2 Esdras 7 and 8, 1 Enoch 100, and Wisdom of Solomon 3 beside Matthew 13:47-50
summary_md: *the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind: Which, when it was full, they drew to shore, and sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but cast the bad away. So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just* (Matthew 13:47-49). The dragnet says from the sea what the wheat and tares said from the field a few verses earlier: everything is gathered, and then the angels do the sorting, and not before. Ezra was shown the day the sorting happens, when *the most High shall appear upon the seat of judgment, and misery shall pass away, and the long suffering shall have an end: But judgment only shall remain* (2 Esdras 7:33-34), and he was told how the count comes out: *many be created, but few shall be saved* (2 Esdras 8:3). Enoch was shown the same day from the other side of it, from where the righteous stand while the angels go to work on the sinners: *In those days the angels shall descend into the secret places And gather together into one place all those who brought down sin, And the El Elyon (Most High) will arise on that day of judgement To execute great judgement amongst sinners.* (1 Enoch 100:4), *And over all the righteous and holy He will appoint guardians from amongst the holy angels To guard them as the apple of an eye, Until He makes an end of all wickedness and all sin, And though the righteous sleep a long sleep, they have nought to fear.* (1 Enoch 100:5). The good are gathered into vessels and kept; the bad are cast away; and the righteous who have been asleep in the dust the whole time have nothing to fear from the day. What comes after the sorting is the reign, when the Wisdom of Solomon says of the righteous that *they shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). That is the gathered remnant serving as a kingdom of priests to the nations left after the judgement. The net, the seat of judgement, the guardians over the righteous and the dominion of the saints are one day told four ways.

title: The wicked husbandmen — prophets slain, house desolate, corrupt shepherds judged, and the tribes of Ya'aqov (Jacob) gathered as from the beginning
summary_md: The vineyard is Isaiah's, the vineyard of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) which is the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and the husbandmen who beat and kill the owner's servants are the men entrusted with it, the leadership, not the people of the vineyard. The servants are the prophets, and the killing is the pattern the whole Tanakh records. Ezra heard the Father name it: *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands* (2 Esdras 1:32), and name its consequence: *your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble* (2 Esdras 1:33), which is what Yahusha (Jesus) says to the city at the end of chapter 23 and shows the disciples at the start of chapter 24. Last of all the owner sends his son, and the crowd itself pronounces the sentence: *They say unto him, He will miserably destroy those wicked men, and will let out his vineyard unto other husbandmen, which shall render him the fruits in their seasons.* (Matthew 21:41). Enoch watched that sentence carried out in the dream of the sheep. The Lord of the sheep handed his flock to seventy shepherds with a count of how many might be destroyed, *And I saw till those shepherds pastured in their season, and they began to slay and to destroy more than they were bidden, and they delivered those sheep into the hand of the lions.* (1 Enoch 89:65), and in the end *And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were cast into that fiery abyss.* (1 Enoch 90:25). Then comes the verse the pulpit turned into replacement: *the kingdom of Elohim (God) shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.* A nation, one, singular in the Greek. Not the Gentile church in place of Yashar'el (Israel); the stewardship taken from the men who held it and given to the fruit-bearing remnant of both houses, gathered as the prophets said. Sirach prayed for exactly that: *gather all the tribes of Ya'aqov (Jacob) together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). The stone the builders rejected becomes the head of the corner, and the vineyard goes to the tribes brought home.

title: Wisdom hidden from the wicked and revealed to the elect — 1 Enoch 48, 2 Esdras 5, Wisdom of Solomon 1, and Sirach 39 beside Matthew 13:10-17
summary_md: When the disciples ask why he speaks to the crowds in parables, Yahusha (Jesus) answers with a passive verb: *He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.* (Matthew 13:11). It has been given, before the hearing, and then he quotes Isaiah 6: *they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.* The giving comes first, and the hearing shows who received it. Enoch was shown the same order at the fountain of wisdom: *And the wisdom of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath revealed him to the holy and righteous; For he hath preserved the lot of the righteous, Because they have hated and despised this world of unrighteousness, And have hated all its works and ways in the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits: For in his name they are saved, And according to his good pleasure hath it been in regard to their life.* (1 Enoch 48:7). The Son is revealed to the holy and righteous whose lot the Father preserved, according to his good pleasure. The rest of the library says it from the other side. The Wisdom of Solomon warns that *into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject unto sin* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:4). Ezra is told that in the last days wisdom and understanding withdraw into their secret chamber and are sought of many and not found (2 Esdras 5:9-10). Sirach says the spirit of understanding is poured out on the scribe when the great Yahuah (LORD) wills it (Ecclesiasticus 39:6). The Father does not slam a door on anyone; the soul that loves its sin closes itself, and wisdom, meeting the closed door, passes by. So the disciples do not earn the mysteries by being clever, and the crowd does not lose them by being dull. The ones who hear were given to hear, and the hearing reveals what was already true of them. That is what he means when he says elsewhere that his sheep hear his voice.

title: The souls of the righteous in the hand of Elohim
summary_md: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1) — *In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery,* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:2) *And their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:3). It ain't new: the seer of the seals sees these very souls — *I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of Elohim (God), and for the testimony which they held* (Revelation 6:9), and a voice from heaven seals it, *Blessed are the dead which die in Yahuah (Lord) from henceforth... that they may rest from their labours* (Revelation 14:13). And Enoch had read their portion off the heavenly tablets: *That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours, And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living. And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice, And their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One Unto all the generations of the world: wherefore no longer fear their contumely.* (1 Enoch 103:3-4). The grave is not destruction but peace; the hand that holds them is Yahuah's own.

title: The righteous dead condemns the ungodly
summary_md: The chapter ends at the judgment scene: *Thus the righteous that is dead shall condemn the ungodly which are living; and youth that is soon perfected the many years and old age of the unrighteous* (Wisdom of Solomon 4:16). The ungodly who once despised him now see him vindicated and are themselves derided: *They shall see him, and despise him; but Yahuah (God) shall laugh them to scorn: and they shall hereafter be a vile carcase, and a reproach among the dead for evermore* (Wisdom of Solomon 4:18). That scorning laugh is the Psalmist's enthroned Yahuah: *He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: Yahuah (Lord) shall have them in derision* (Psalm 2:4). And the next chapter delivers the too-late confession the ungodly will groan — the Wisdom of Solomon's own continuation, the kings and the mighty seeing the vindicated righteous too late: *And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach* (The Wisdom of Solomon 5:3), *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour* (The Wisdom of Solomon 5:4). It ain't new — it is the same too-late awakening Enoch saw come over the kings and the mighty when they stand before the Son of Adam on the throne of his glory (1 Enoch 62-63), and the same cry John heard from the kings of the earth hiding in the rocks: *And said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sits on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb:* (Revelation 6:16).

title: Woe against those who alter the words and teach men so
summary_md: *Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 5:19). Two things are judged together: breaking a commandment, and teaching others that it may be broken. Enoch pronounces the woe on exactly that pair. *Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness, And transgress the eternal law, And transform themselves into what they were not [into sinners]: They shall be trodden under foot upon the earth.* (1 Enoch 99:2). The law is called eternal, and the sin is perverting its words, which is what a man does when he teaches that the least of them no longer binds. Enoch goes after the ones who put it in writing too: *Woe to you who write down lying and godless words; for they write down their lies that men may hear them and act godlessly towards (their) neighbour.* (1 Enoch 98:15), and the ones who bear false witness to it: *Woe to you, lying witnesses, And to those who weigh out injustice, For suddenly shall ye perish.* (1 Enoch 95:6). He even foresaw the alteration of the Father's own reckoning of days and seasons: *Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.* (1 Enoch 82:5). The pulpit that tells a congregation the Sabbath was moved, the feasts were done away, and the food laws were nailed to a cross is breaking the least commandments and teaching men so, and the two registers, Enoch's woe and the King's measure of who is least in the kingdom, name it the same way. The people in the pews were handed it; the woe is on the ones doing the teaching.

title: Woes on the rich and riches cannot save — 1 Enoch 94-100 beside Matthew 19:23-26
summary_md: *Then said Yahusha (Jesus) unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven. And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God).* (Matthew 19:23-24). The disciples are staggered, *Who then can be saved?*, because they had been taught that wealth was the sign of the Father's favor, and he answers, *With men this is impossible; but with Elohim (God) all things are possible.* (Matthew 19:26). Enoch's last chapters are a long string of woes against the very trust the young ruler had just walked away with. *Woe to you, ye rich, for ye have trusted in your riches, And from your riches shall ye depart, Because ye have not remembered the El Elyon (Most High) in the days of your riches.* (1 Enoch 94:8). He puts the rich man's own words in his mouth: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: 'We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired. And now let us do what we purposed: For we have gathered silver, And many are the husbandmen in our houses.' And our granaries are (brim) full as with water,* (1 Enoch 97:8-9), which is the rich fool of Luke 12 word for word, *This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods.* (Luke 12:18). And he says why the money cannot help on the day it matters: *And now, know ye that ye are prepared for the day of destruction: wherefore do not hope to live, ye sinners, but ye shall depart and die; for ye know no ransom; for ye are prepared for the day of the great judgement, for the day of tribulation and great shame for your spirits.* (1 Enoch 98:10); *And (then) the children of the earth shall see the wise in security, And shall understand all the words of this book, And recognize that their riches shall not be able to save them In the overthrow of their sins.* (1 Enoch 100:6). The Psalm had said it before Enoch's book was read in Galilee: *None of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to Elohim (God) a ransom for him:* (Psalm 49:7). There was no little gate in Jerusalem called the Needle's Eye; the saying means what it says. And it does not turn Abraham's flocks or the blessings of Deuteronomy 28 into a curse; those came to men whose heart was with Yahuah (God). It is the trust that damns, and the only ransom that counts is the one the Son of Adam came to pay.
